note: PLAA-related disorder presents primarily as a neurodegenerative/neurodevelopmental disorder restricted to the central nervous system without major extraneural structural malformations.

evidence.text: Affected patients presented with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay characterized as a leukoencephalopathy without reported extraneural structural anomalies.

source.title: Phospholipase A2-activating protein is associated with a novel form of leukoencephalopathy
source.quote: Herein, we have identified a unique form of leukoencephalopathy in seven patients presenting at ages 2 to 4 months with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay.

evidence.text: PLAA mutations cause an infantile neurodysfunction syndrome characterized by synaptic trafficking defects, progressive microcephaly, and seizures rather than systemic or extra-CNS organ malformations.

source.title: PLAA mutations cause a lethal infantile epileptic encephalopathy by disrupting ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation of synaptic proteins
source.quote: In both human and mouse, hypomorphic mutations in the ubiquitin adaptor protein PLAA cause an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome with seizures.
